```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
PKNCA::PKNCA.options(progress = FALSE)
```

# Model and source

```{r models}
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hanke_2026_iclepertin"))
mod_pd <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hanke_2026_iclepertin_hemoglobin"))
```

* Citation: `r mod_pd$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2026.1770980>
* Supplementary Material (population PK parameter table S2, steady-state
  exposure table S3 and the NONMEM control stream of the hemoglobin model):
  <https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fphar.2026.1770980/full#supplementary-material>

Hanke 2026 assessed the anemia risk of long-term treatment with iclepertin
(BI 425809), a glycine transporter 1 (GlyT1) inhibitor developed for cognitive
impairment associated with schizophrenia (CIAS). GlyT1 inhibition limits the
glycine available to erythroid precursors for heme synthesis, so the drug
lowers the hemoglobin content of newly formed red blood cells. The analysis was
sequential, and the paper contributes two models:

* `Hanke_2026_iclepertin` -- the population PK model (Supplementary Table S2):

  > `r mod_pk$description`

* `Hanke_2026_iclepertin_hemoglobin` -- the semi-mechanistic hemoglobin model
  (Table 2 and the control stream), driven by the individual steady-state AUC
  that the PK model provides:

  > `r mod_pd$description`

# Population

**PK model.** Nine studies, 1031 subjects (placebo excluded): seven Phase I
studies in healthy volunteers (single and multiple rising dose, proof of
mechanism, Japanese and Chinese single rising dose, an itraconazole
interaction study, absolute bioavailability and human ADME; 0.5-150 mg) and two
12-week Phase II studies at 2-25 mg once daily in CIAS (n = 325) and
Alzheimer's disease (n = 477) patients (Supplementary Table S1). The paper does
not tabulate demographics for the PK dataset.

**Hemoglobin model.** Three studies with long-term hematology, 1116 subjects
after excluding ten outliers (Table 1, Supplementary Table S6): a 14-day
proof-of-mechanism study in 25 healthy volunteers (5-50 mg) and the two 12-week
Phase II studies (placebo and 2-25 mg) in 492 CIAS and 599 Alzheimer's disease
patients. MCH and RBC were fitted simultaneously (12328 observations).
Continuous covariates were normalised to age 59 years, BMI 26.8 kg/m^2 and ALT
18 U/L. Phase III CONNEX-1/-2/-3 data (821 CIAS patients on 10 mg for 26 weeks)
served as external validation.

```{r population}
pop_table <- function(pop) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Field = names(pop),
    Value = vapply(pop, function(x) paste(as.character(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
  )
}
knitr::kable(pop_table(mod_pk$population), caption = "PK model population metadata.")
knitr::kable(pop_table(mod_pd$population), caption = "Hemoglobin model population metadata.")
```

## Hemoglobin model (`Hanke_2026_iclepertin_hemoglobin`)

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lmtt_rbc` | log(126) day, fixed | Table 2; control stream THETA(1) 126 FIX |
| `lkin_mch` | log(0.244) pg/cell/day | Table 2 |
| `lkin_rbc` | log(0.0351) 10^12/L/day | Table 2 |
| `lemax` | log(0.552) | Table 2 |
| `lauc50` | log(43500) nmol*h/L | Table 2 |
| `fb` | -1.41 | Table 2 |
| `e_age_kin_mch`, `e_bmi_kin_mch`, `e_race_black_kin_mch` | 0.0235, -0.0583, 0.948 | Table 2; control stream THETA(15), (12), (10) |
| `e_sexm_kin_rbc`, `e_age_kin_rbc`, `e_bmi_kin_rbc`, `e_race_asian_kin_rbc`, `e_alt_kin_rbc` | 1.07, -0.0592, 0.0451, 0.970, 0.0169 | Table 2; control stream THETA(7), (11), (13), (14), (16) |
| `etalkin_mch`, `etalkin_rbc`, `etalauc50`, `etafb` | log(1 + CV^2) of 5.76, 7.49, 83.0, 79.7 % | Table 2 (CV% footnote) |
| `addSd_MCH`, `addSd_RBC` | 0.522 pg, 0.159 10^12/L | Table 2; control stream THETA(8), THETA(9) with $SIGMA 1 FIX |
| `ktr = 4 / lifespan` | n/a | Results "Final model"; control stream $PK |
| `d/dt(mch1) = Kin_MCH (1 - Emax AUC / (AUC50 + AUC)) - ktr mch1` | n/a | Results equation; control stream DADT(1) |
| `d/dt(erythrocytes1) = Kin_RBC_0 (HB / HB_0)^Feedbk - ktr erythrocytes1` | n/a | Results equation; control stream DADT(5) |
| transit chains, steady-state initial conditions, `HB_0` | n/a | control stream $PK (A_0) and $DES |
| `thb` = sum of MCH_i x RBC_i | n/a | Figure 1 |

# Simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
# Iclepertin molecular weight (C20H18F6N2O5S), used only to convert the PK
# model's ng/mL output to the nmol/L and nmol*h/L units of the paper. The paper
# does not print it.
mw_iclepertin <- 512.4

# Hemoglobin event frame: observations only (no dosing compartment); iclepertin
# acts through the AUC_ICLEPERTIN covariate, which switches off 48 h after the
# last dose (Results "Final model"). All endpoints are algebraic sums of the
# states, so observation rows carry dvid = 1 with cmt = NA and every output is
# returned on every row.
pd_events <- function(cov, auc, t_off = 366, times = seq(0, 540, by = 5)) {
  times <- sort(unique(c(times, t_off)))
  tidyr::crossing(cov, time = times) |>
    dplyr::left_join(auc, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      AUC_ICLEPERTIN = ifelse(time < t_off, auc_on, 0),
      evid = 0L,
      cmt = NA_character_,
      dvid = 1L
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-auc_on) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

pd_solve <- function(model, events, keep = NULL) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    model, events = events, keep = keep,
    covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}

ref_patient <- function(id = 1L, SEXF = 0L) {
  # Reference patient of Figure 2: White, 38 years, BMI 29.1 kg/m^2, ALT 21 U/L.
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id, SEXF = SEXF, AGE = 38, BMI = 29.1, ALT = 21,
    RACE_BLACK = 0L, RACE_ASIAN = 0L
  )
}

# Typical-value solve: every eta supplied as a zero column with omega = NA,
# which is deterministic for any number of subjects.
pd_solve_typ <- function(events) {
  events[c("etalkin_mch", "etalkin_rbc", "etalauc50", "etafb")] <- 0
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_pd, events = events, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
    covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame"
  )
}
```

# Population PK model

## Typical steady-state profile

```{r pk-typical}
pk_cohort <- function(n, dose, id_offset = 0L) {
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    dose_grp = paste(dose, "mg"),
    DOSE = dose,
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 38, 9), 18), 55),
    WT = exp(rnorm(n, log(85), 0.18)),
    RACE_BLACK = rbinom(n, 1, 0.2),
    RACE_ASIAN = 0L,
    RACE_OTHER = 0L,
    SMOKE = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5),
    FED = 0L,
    DIS_HEALTHY = 0L
  )
}

pk_events <- function(cohort) {
  # 14 once-daily doses; dense sampling over the last 24 h interval
  # (steady state: the terminal half-life is 33-47 h).
  doses <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 13 * 24, by = 24)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = DOSE, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = 13 * 24 + c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.25), seq(5, 24, by = 1))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

typ <- pk_events(tibble::tibble(
  id = 1L, dose_grp = "10 mg", DOSE = 10, AGE = 38, WT = 85, RACE_BLACK = 0L,
  RACE_ASIAN = 0L, RACE_OTHER = 0L, SMOKE = 0L, FED = 0L, DIS_HEALTHY = 0L
))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk), events = typ, returnType = "data.frame")

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time - 13 * 24, Cc * 1000 / mw_iclepertin)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the 14th daily dose (h)", y = "Iclepertin (nmol/L)",
    title = "Typical 10 mg once-daily steady-state profile",
    caption = "Fasted CIAS patient, 38 years, 85 kg, White, non-smoker."
  )
```

## Steady-state exposure in a virtual Phase II CIAS cohort (Table S3)

Supplementary Table S3 gives the geometric mean steady-state AUC, Cmax and
trough for the Phase II CIAS population at each dose. The paper does not report
the demographics of that population beyond the Figure 2 reference patient
(38 years, BMI 29.1 kg/m^2), so the cohort below is an approximation: 200
patients per dose, age normal around 38 years (18-55), weight log-normal around
85 kg, 20% Black, half smokers, all fasted.

```{r pk-cohort}
set.seed(20261770)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261770)
cohort_pk <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  pk_cohort(200, 2, id_offset = 0L),
  pk_cohort(200, 5, id_offset = 200L),
  pk_cohort(200, 10, id_offset = 400L),
  pk_cohort(200, 25, id_offset = 600L)
)
ev_pk <- pk_events(cohort_pk)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_pk[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = ev_pk, keep = "dose_grp", returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r pk-nca}
t_start <- 13 * 24
conc_nca <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, dose_grp, time, Cc = Cc * 1000 / mw_iclepertin)
dose_nca <- ev_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, dose_grp, time, amt)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = t_start, end = t_start + 24,
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | dose_grp + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | dose_grp + id),
  intervals = intervals
))

# Supplementary Table S3: geometric means (CV%) for the Phase II CIAS population.
published_s3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_grp, ~auclast, ~cmax, ~cmin,
  "2 mg",    929,      50.1,  29.2,
  "5 mg",    2090,     113,   65.1,
  "10 mg",   4020,     222,   121,
  "25 mg",   8390,     462,   255
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_s3,
  by = "dose_grp",
  units = c(auclast = "nmol*h/L", cmax = "nmol/L", cmin = "nmol/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated (median) vs. published (geometric mean) steady-state exposure, Supplementary Table S3. * differs by more than 20%."
)
```

```{r pk-gate}
# Closed-form steady-state AUC (F * dose / CL) at the cohort's median
# covariates, independent of the random draw. A mis-transcribed CL, F or unit
# moves this by tens of percent.
auc_closed <- function(dose, f) {
  cl <- 3.98 * (85 / 70)^0.164 * (38 / 40)^-1.64
  f * dose / cl * 1e6 / mw_iclepertin
}
closed <- c(
  "2 mg" = auc_closed(2, 1), "5 mg" = auc_closed(5, 1),
  "10 mg" = auc_closed(10, 0.931), "25 mg" = auc_closed(25, 0.823)
)
pct_closed <- 100 * (closed - published_s3$auclast) / published_s3$auclast
round(pct_closed, 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(pct_closed) < 15))
```

The closed-form typical AUCs lie within about 10% of Table S3 at every dose.
This depends on the assumed reference age of 40 years (see Assumptions and
deviations). With an exponent of -1.64, each 10% shift of the reference age
moves the typical clearance by about 17%. Only the AUC and trough are
interpretable here. The simulated Cmax also depends on the assumed fasted state
(`FED` raises KA 1.68-fold) and on the direction of the diagnosis effect on
KA.

# Hemoglobin model

## Homeostasis without drug

```{r pd-homeostasis}
ev0 <- pd_events(ref_patient(), tibble::tibble(id = 1L, auc_on = 0))
s0 <- pd_solve_typ(ev0)
drift <- max(abs(s0$thb - s0$thb[1])) / s0$thb[1]
c(baseline_hb = s0$thb[1], baseline_mch = s0$MCH[1], baseline_rbc = s0$RBC[1], max_rel_drift = drift)
stopifnot(drift < 1e-6)
```

The typical male reference patient has a baseline MCH of
`r round(s0$MCH[1], 2)` pg, RBC of `r round(s0$RBC[1], 2)` x 10^12/L and
hemoglobin of `r round(s0$thb[1], 1)` g/L.

## Reference-patient decreases (Results "Model-based simulations")

The paper reports relative decreases of 2.0% at 10 mg (typical AUC 4020
nmol*h/L) and 7.6% at a fivefold higher exposure, equal to 2.9 / 11.3 g/L for
the male and 2.7 / 10.5 g/L for the female reference patient.

```{r pd-reference}
ref_cov <- dplyr::bind_rows(ref_patient(1L, 0L), ref_patient(2L, 0L), ref_patient(3L, 1L), ref_patient(4L, 1L))
ref_auc <- tibble::tibble(id = 1:4, auc_on = c(4020, 5 * 4020, 4020, 5 * 4020))
s_ref <- pd_solve_typ(pd_events(ref_cov, ref_auc))

ref_tab <- s_ref |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    base = thb[time == 0][1],
    day365 = thb[time == 365][1],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sex = c("male", "male", "female", "female"),
    exposure = c("10 mg", "5-fold", "10 mg", "5-fold"),
    pct = 100 * (base - day365) / base,
    abs = base - day365,
    pct_paper = c(2.0, 7.6, 2.0, 7.6),
    abs_paper = c(2.9, 11.3, 2.7, 10.5)
  )
ref_tab |>
  dplyr::select(sex, exposure, base, day365, pct, pct_paper, abs, abs_paper) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Sex" = sex, "Exposure" = exposure, "Baseline Hb (g/L)" = base,
    "Day-365 Hb (g/L)" = day365, "Decrease (%)" = pct, "Paper (%)" = pct_paper,
    "Decrease (g/L)" = abs, "Paper (g/L)" = abs_paper
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical reference-patient hemoglobin decreases after 365 days.")

# Same parameters, closed-form steady state: (HB/HB0)^(1 - Feedbk) = 1 - INH.
inh <- function(auc) 0.552 * auc / (43500 + auc)
ss_pct <- 100 * (1 - (1 - inh(c(4020, 20100)))^(1 / (1 + 1.41)))
round(ss_pct, 2)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ref_tab$pct - ref_tab$pct_paper) < 0.15),
  all(abs(ref_tab$abs - ref_tab$abs_paper) < 0.15),
  all(abs(ref_tab$pct - rep(ss_pct, 2)) < 0.05)
)
```

The day-365 hemoglobin reproduces both the percentages and the absolute
decreases to within the paper's rounding. The female fivefold value is 10.6 g/L
against the printed 10.5.

## Covariate effects on baseline (Discussion)

The Discussion states that Black and Asian race lower hemoglobin by 5.2% and
3.0%. Both effects act on baseline production, so at baseline they equal the
Kin factors (0.948 on MCH, 0.970 on RBC).

```{r pd-race}
race_cov <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ref_patient(1L),
  ref_patient(2L) |> dplyr::mutate(RACE_BLACK = 1L),
  ref_patient(3L) |> dplyr::mutate(RACE_ASIAN = 1L)
)
s_race <- pd_solve_typ(pd_events(race_cov, tibble::tibble(id = 1:3, auc_on = 0), times = 0))
race_pct <- 100 * (1 - s_race$thb[s_race$time == 0][2:3] / s_race$thb[s_race$time == 0][1])
round(race_pct, 2)
stopifnot(abs(race_pct[1] - 5.2) < 0.1, abs(race_pct[2] - 3.0) < 0.1)
```

## Maximum effect (Discussion "Model parameter estimates")

At an exposure far above AUC50 the inhibition approaches Emax = 0.552. The
paper reports that the maximum predicted hemoglobin decrease "approached ~25%".

```{r pd-emax}
auc_grid <- c(4020, 20100, 43500, 1e5, 1e6)
tibble::tibble(
  `AUC (nmol*h/L)` = auc_grid,
  `Inhibition of Kin_MCH` = inh(auc_grid),
  `Steady-state Hb decrease (%)` = 100 * (1 - (1 - inh(auc_grid))^(1 / 2.41))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Replication of Figure 3

Figure 3 shows 365 days at 10 mg daily or fivefold exposure, then 175 days off
treatment, by sex. The paper resampled 1000 Phase III patients per sex, whose
covariates are not published. The virtual cohort below uses 200 patients per
sex and scenario. Individual AUC is log-normal around the Table S3 geometric mean
(4020 nmol*h/L, 64.5% CV), multiplied by 5 in the high-exposure arm. Age is
normal around 37 years (18-55), BMI log-normal around 29.1 kg/m^2, ALT
log-normal around 21 U/L, and the cohort is 75% White, 20% Black and 5% Asian.

```{r fig3-sim}
set.seed(20261771)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261771)
make_pd_cohort <- function(n, sexf, scenario, mult, id_offset) {
  sd_auc <- sqrt(log(1 + 0.645^2))
  race <- sample(c("W", "B", "A"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.75, 0.2, 0.05))
  cov <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    sex = ifelse(sexf == 1, "Female", "Male"),
    scenario = scenario,
    SEXF = sexf,
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 37, 10), 18), 55),
    BMI = exp(rnorm(n, log(29.1), 0.18)),
    ALT = exp(rnorm(n, log(21), 0.45)),
    RACE_BLACK = as.integer(race == "B"),
    RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "A")
  )
  auc <- tibble::tibble(id = cov$id, auc_on = mult * exp(rnorm(n, log(4020), sd_auc)))
  pd_events(cov, auc, times = seq(0, 540, by = 10))
}
ev_fig3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_pd_cohort(200, 0, "10 mg daily", 1, 0L),
  make_pd_cohort(200, 1, "10 mg daily", 1, 200L),
  make_pd_cohort(200, 0, "Fivefold higher exposure", 5, 400L),
  make_pd_cohort(200, 1, "Fivefold higher exposure", 5, 600L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_fig3[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
sim_fig3 <- pd_solve(mod_pd, ev_fig3, keep = c("sex", "scenario"))

q_fig3 <- sim_fig3 |>
  dplyr::group_by(sex, scenario, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q025 = quantile(thb, 0.025), Q50 = median(thb), Q975 = quantile(thb, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(q_fig3, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q025, ymax = Q975), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q025), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q975), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_grid(scenario ~ factor(sex, levels = c("Male", "Female"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 540, by = 90)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(90, 190)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Hemoglobin (g/L)",
    title = "Hemoglobin at 10 mg daily or fivefold higher exposure",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Hanke 2026 (median and 2.5th-97.5th percentiles; treatment stops at day 364)."
  )
```

```{r fig3-check}
fig3_tab <- q_fig3 |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0, 360, 540)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(scenario, sex, time)
knitr::kable(fig3_tab, digits = 1, caption = "Simulated hemoglobin percentiles (g/L).")

below100 <- sim_fig3 |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 360) |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, sex) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pct_below_100 = 100 * mean(thb < 100), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(below100, digits = 1, caption = "Virtual patients below 100 g/L on day 360.")

med <- function(sc, sx, t) q_fig3$Q50[q_fig3$scenario == sc & q_fig3$sex == sx & q_fig3$time == t]
drop_pct <- c(
  male_10 = 100 * (1 - med("10 mg daily", "Male", 360) / med("10 mg daily", "Male", 0)),
  male_5x = 100 * (1 - med("Fivefold higher exposure", "Male", 360) / med("Fivefold higher exposure", "Male", 0))
)
round(drop_pct, 2)
stopifnot(
  # Baseline medians sit near the typical values (148 male, 138 female g/L);
  # Figure 3 shows about 150 and 138.
  abs(med("10 mg daily", "Male", 0) - 148) < 5,
  abs(med("10 mg daily", "Female", 0) - 138) < 5,
  # The median drop tracks the typical-value 2% / 7.6%; IIV on AUC50 and the
  # feedback widens it only slightly.
  abs(drop_pct[["male_10"]] - 2) < 1.5,
  abs(drop_pct[["male_5x"]] - 7.6) < 2.5,
  # Recovery: back to within 1% of baseline 175 days after stopping.
  abs(med("Fivefold higher exposure", "Male", 540) / med("Fivefold higher exposure", "Male", 0) - 1) < 0.01
)
```

As in Figure 3, the new steady state is reached after about 120-140 days, and
recovery after stopping is as slow as the decline. At 10 mg daily no virtual
patient falls below 100 g/L. The paper reports that more than 97.5% of patients
stay above 100 g/L even at fivefold exposure, and its Figure 3 places the
female 2.5th percentile just above the threshold (about 101 g/L). In this
cohort the high-exposure female 2.5th percentile is a few g/L lower (about 96
g/L, with about 4-5% below 100 g/L). This is a lower tail of a cohort whose
covariates are assumed: the paper resampled the unpublished Phase III
demographics, which were less variable than the Phase II data (Discussion). The
fraction below 100 g/L is therefore reported and not asserted. The medians and
the typical-value decreases match.

## Subgroups (Figures 4 and 5)

Figures 4 and 5 vary race and age for male and female patients at 10 mg daily.
The typical values below show the same ordering: female, Black and older
patients start lower, and every subgroup loses about 2% over a year.

```{r fig45}
grid <- tidyr::crossing(
  SEXF = c(0L, 1L), race = c("White", "Black", "Asian"), AGE = c(20, 38, 65, 90)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(), BMI = 29.1, ALT = 21,
    RACE_BLACK = as.integer(race == "Black"), RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "Asian")
  )
s_grid <- pd_solve_typ(
  pd_events(grid |> dplyr::select(-race), tibble::tibble(id = grid$id, auc_on = 4020), times = c(0, 365))
)
grid_tab <- s_grid |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(base = thb[time == 0][1], day365 = thb[time == 365][1], .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(grid, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(sex = ifelse(SEXF == 1, "female", "male"), pct = 100 * (base - day365) / base) |>
  dplyr::select(sex, race, AGE, base, day365, pct)
grid_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Sex" = sex, "Race" = race, "Age (y)" = AGE, "Baseline Hb (g/L)" = base, "Day-365 Hb (g/L)" = day365, "Decrease (%)" = pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical hemoglobin at 10 mg daily (BMI 29.1, ALT 21).")
stopifnot(all(abs(grid_tab$pct - 1.96) < 0.1))
```

The decrease is the same 1.96% in every subgroup. This follows from the model
structure: covariates enter only through the production rates, and the
steady-state relative change depends only on Emax, AUC50 and the feedback
exponent.

## Linking the PK and hemoglobin models

The PK model supplies `AUC_ICLEPERTIN` as `fdepot * dose / cl`. The paper used
individual empirical Bayes estimates. For a typical fasted CIAS patient (38
years, 85 kg, White) at 10 mg once daily, the value converted to nmol*h/L is:

```{r link}
cl_typ <- 3.98 * (85 / 70)^0.164 * (38 / 40)^-1.64
auc_link <- 0.931 * 10 / cl_typ * 1e6 / mw_iclepertin
auc_link
s_link <- pd_solve_typ(pd_events(ref_patient(), tibble::tibble(id = 1L, auc_on = auc_link), times = c(0, 365)))
100 * (1 - s_link$thb[s_link$time == 365] / s_link$thb[s_link$time == 0])
```

# Assumptions and deviations

## PK model reporting gaps

* **Reference weight.** Supplementary Table S2 gives power exponents for body
  weight but not the reference weight; 70 kg is assumed.
* **Age effect.** Table S2 reports "Effect of age on CL" = -1.64 without the
  functional form or the reference age. A normalised power model
  `(AGE / 40)^-1.64` is assumed. This is the form the paper states for its
  continuous PD covariates, and an exponential-linear form with this coefficient
  would be implausible. 40 years was taken as a round adult reference. With it,
  the closed-form typical AUCs agree with Table S3 to within about 10% for a
  38-year-old patient. The reference age is not a published value, and
  steady-state AUC predictions scale with it: each 10% change in the reference
  age moves CL/F by about 17%.
* **Diagnosis effect on KA.** Table S2 lists "Effect of diagnosis on KA" = 2.31
  without the coding. The factor is applied to patients with a diagnosis (CIAS
  or Alzheimer's disease) relative to healthy volunteers, via `DIS_HEALTHY`.
  This affects only the absorption rate (Cmax and Tmax), not the steady-state AUC
  that drives the hemoglobin model.
* **Dose-level bioavailability.** Table S2 gives relative bioavailabilities for
  10 mg (0.931) and 25 mg (0.823) doses. Doses below 10 mg are taken as the
  reference (F = 1). Doses of 50 mg and above (Phase I only) are assigned the
  25 mg value, and intermediate doses take the band below them.
* **Race categories.** White is the reference; Black, Asian and Other carry the
  Table S2 factors (Asian = 1.00 was estimated, so it is kept).
* **Concentration units.** The model reports ng/mL (dose in mg). The paper's
  tables are in nmol/L and nmol*h/L. This vignette converts with the iclepertin
  molecular weight of 512.4 g/mol (C20H18F6N2O5S), which the paper does not
  print.

## Hemoglobin model

* **Residual error.** The control stream annotates THETA(8) and THETA(9) as
  "(pg/cell)^2" and "(10^12/L)^2", and a commented-out `$SIGMA` line converts
  0.522 to an SD of 0.722. However, the fitted error model is
  `Y = IPRED + W * EPS(1)` with `W = THETA(8)` (or THETA(9)) and `$SIGMA 1 FIX`.
  That makes the THETAs standard deviations, matching the "(pg/cell)" and
  "(10^12/L)" units of Table 2. The packaged model uses 0.522 pg and
  0.159 x 10^12/L as additive SDs, following the code.
* **Fixed-zero random effects.** The control stream carries `$OMEGA 0 FIX` on
  the RBC lifespan and on Emax. These etas are omitted.
* **Control stream comment labels.** The `$THETA` comments label THETA(12) as
  "BMI on KinMCH" and THETA(11) as "AGE on KinRBC", consistent with `$PK` and
  Table 2. The packaged model follows `$PK`.
* **Total hemoglobin output.** In the control stream each MCH compartment holds
  one quarter of the cell's hemoglobin content (the observed MCH is their sum),
  so the `$DES` sum of MCH_i x RBC_i is one quarter of total hemoglobin; only its
  ratio to baseline enters the feedback. The `thb` output multiplies it by four,
  giving Figure 1's total hemoglobin with MCH_i as the per-cell content. At
  steady state this equals MCH x RBC, the definition of observed hemoglobin in
  the Supplementary Material.
* **Exposure time course.** `AUC_ICLEPERTIN` is a step covariate: the
  individual AUCtau,ss from the first dose, zero 48 h after the last dose
  (Results "Final model"). The user encodes this time course; the simulations
  here use last-observation-carried-forward interpolation.
* **Validation against Phase III (Figure 6).** This needs the unpublished
  individual CONNEX data and is not reproduced.

## Virtual cohorts

The Phase II CIAS and Phase III demographics are not published beyond the
reference patient (male, White, 38 years, BMI 29.1 kg/m^2, ALT 21 U/L). The
distributions of age, weight, BMI, ALT, race, smoking and food status used
above are assumptions. They affect the spread of the virtual cohorts, not the
typical-value checks. No correction notice for the article was found as of
2026-11-14.
